content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) does not recommend the use of ACE inhibitors or ARBs solely for the primary prevention of diabetic kidney disease in patients who are normotensive. Instead, the emphasis is placed on achieving optimal blood glucose control, with an A1C target of 7%, and maintaining blood pressure within a target of less than 130/80 mmHg. This preventive strategy prioritizes the management of existing conditions that contribute to the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), rather than relying on medications that may pose potential adverse effects in patients who do not have established kidney damage.
